text: CHAPTER 31
speaker: Narrator

text: The Name That Was Crossed Out
speaker: Narrator
note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

text: The wall behind the kneeling statue began to open without a sound.
speaker: Narrator

text: White limestone parted along a seam that had not existed a breath earlier. Cold air moved out of the darkness beyond, carrying the same faint scent of ozone and old copper that clung to the ledger chamber. The statue rose and stepped aside with the same unthinking precision it had shown since the corridor first closed behind them.
speaker: Narrator

text: They entered.
speaker: Narrator

text: The chamber beyond was larger than the name corridor and colder. The walls here were still white limestone, still covered in rows of personal names, but the cuts were deeper and the crossed-out lines more frequent. Condensation wept down the stone in thin sheets that smelled of a forge just before the metal comes out of the fire, though there was no heat—only cold that behaved as if it remembered being hot.
speaker: Narrator

text: The grain beneath the moisture slid like sand in an hourglass. Looking away and looking back had become its own kind of danger.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik found himself staring at a jagged, freshly etched stroke that looked like a scar cut into the stone.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag,
speaker: Zik

text: he said. His voice sounded strangely distant even to himself.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: It's your name. It's crossed out.
speaker: Zik

text: Balag stepped forward. His face had gone pale. He was not a man who scared easily—Zik had seen him stand his ground against things with teeth and things with blades and things that were neither—but there was a particular kind of fear that came from being told your own name was written somewhere you could not see it, and that fear had him now.
speaker: Narrator

text: You're losing your mind, Zik,
speaker: Balag

text: he said, though there was no real conviction behind it.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: There's nothing there but a blur.
speaker: Balag

text: He leaned closer anyway.
speaker: Narrator

text: The stone under Zik's gaze continued to rearrange itself. The crossed-out name that had looked like Balag's a moment earlier was already softening into something else. A different set of characters rose, then blurred, then settled into a shape Ninsun recognized before anyone else did.
speaker: Narrator

text: She went still.
speaker: Narrator

text: That one is mine.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Enhedu looked from one of them to the other, then at the wall, calculating even without the desire that had once made calculation feel like survival.
speaker: Narrator

text: Both of you can't be right.
speaker: Enhedu
note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

text: We can if the ledger is rewriting itself as we watch,
speaker: Ninsun

text: Ninsun said. Her voice had gone thin.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Or if it is showing each of us the account it intends to close next.
speaker: Ninsun

text: The scraping resumed.
speaker: Narrator

text: Scrape.
speaker: Narrator

text: Pause.
speaker: Narrator

text: Scrape.
speaker: Narrator

text: Pause.
speaker: Narrator

text: It came from everywhere at once—sometimes from the wall ahead, sometimes from beneath the floor, once, impossibly, from somewhere directly behind Zik's eyes, as though the sound had found a way to skip the ears and carve straight into the meat of his skull. He had stopped trying to locate it. Guessing implied the room followed rules the room had already refused.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag backed away from the wall.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: I don't like this place.
speaker: Balag

text: You said that about the last one,
speaker: Enhedu
note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

text: Enhedu answered, but the dryness in her voice was thinner than before.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Zik kept watching the stone. A new name rose under the condensation, held long enough for him to read it, then began to close over itself the way skin closes over a wound. He knew the name. A merchant who sold grain near the Street of Scribes. A man who had once shorted him three measures and laughed when Zik noticed. An ordinary man under an ordinary sky who, at that very moment, was almost certainly still haggling over prices.
speaker: Narrator

text: It looked less like killing than removing the evidence that anyone had ever been known.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun's stylus hovered over parchment that no longer accepted ink the way it once had.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: It's testing which threads it can pull without the fabric noticing.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Balag shook his head hard, as if the motion itself might dislodge something that had begun to settle.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: I don't know what you're talking about. Where is the rest of the crew?
speaker: Balag

text: The question landed harder than any shout could have, because it was not rhetorical. He meant it.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun looked toward the empty space beside them. Recognition broke across her face, incomplete and unstable.
speaker: Narrator

text: Kurash,
speaker: Ninsun

text: she whispered.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Zik followed her gaze. He could almost retrieve the shape—someone younger, ambitious, always calculating his share before the work was finished. The memory arrived in fragments: a voice complaining about the stairs, an extra waterskin that no one had claimed since the ridge, five bedrolls marked in the sand when only four people seemed present. The details had been there the entire time. They had simply stopped belonging to anyone.
speaker: Narrator

text: Enhedu frowned at the empty space.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: I remember a knife. Not the hand that carried it.
speaker: Enhedu
note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

text: Balag stared at them as though they had begun speaking a language he had never learned.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Who?
speaker: Balag
